items.readable_text:
Content:
Consider the integral

Content:
[MATH: \displaystyle \int \dfrac{1}{6x\sqrt{1-36x^2}} \, \textrm{d}x]

Content:
As it is, this integral doesn't resemble any of the basic integrals we have encountered so far. However, we can rewrite our integral as

Content:
[MATH: \int \dfrac{1}{6x\sqrt{1-36x^2}}\,\textrm{d}x = \int \dfrac{1}{(6x)\sqrt{1-\left(6x\right)^2}}\textrm{d}x,]

Content:
which becomes very similar to the basic integral for the inverse hyperbolic secant,
[MATH: \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits}]

Content:
[MATH: \int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-u^2}}\,\textrm{d}u = -\arsech u+C.]

Content:
The only difference is that instead of [MATH: u] as the variable, we have [MATH: 6x.]

Content:
So, let's substitute [MATH: u =6x.] Differentiating, we get

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=6
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\textrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{6} \,\textrm{d}u.]

Content:
Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and compute it, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: ∫(1)/(6xsqrt(1 − 36x^{2}))dx|= ∫(1)/(6xsqrt(1 − (6x)^{2}))dx; = ∫(1)/(usqrt(1 − u^{2})) ⋅ (1)/(6)du; = (1)/(6)∫(1)/(usqrt(1 − u^{2}))du; = − (1)/(6)arsech u + C; = − (1)/(6)arsech (6x) + C]

EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse hyperbolic cosecant,

[MATH: \int rac{1}{|u|\sqrt{1+u^2}}\, extrm{d}u = -\arcsch u+C.]

The only difference is that instead of [MATH: u^2] as the variable, we have [MATH: 9x^2 = (3x)^2.]

So, let's substitute [MATH: u =3x.] Differentiating, we get [MATH: \dfrac{ extrm{d}u}{ extrm{d}x}=3 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad extrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{3} \, extrm{d}u.]

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and compute it, as follows:

[MATH: ∫(1)/(|3x|sqrt(1 + 9x^{2}))dx|= ∫(1)/(|3x|sqrt(1 + (3x)^{2}))dx; = ∫(1)/(|u|sqrt(1 + u^{2})) ⋅ (1)/(3)du; = (1)/(3)∫(1)/(|u|sqrt(1 + u^{2}))du; = − (1)/(3)arcsch u + C; = − (1)/(3)arcsch 3x + C]

EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

Let's rewrite our integral as

[MATH: \int \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{4-x^2}}\, extrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2} \int \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-\left( rac{x}{2} ight)^2}} \, extrm{d}x=\dfrac{1}{4} \int \dfrac{1}{ rac{x}{2}\sqrt{1-\left( rac{x}{2} ight)^2}} \, extrm{d}x.]

This integral resembles the basic integral for the inverse hyperbolic secant,

[MATH: \int rac{1}{u\sqrt{1-u^2}}\, extrm{d}u = -\arsech u+C.]

The only difference is that instead of [MATH: u^2] as the variable, we have [MATH: \left(\dfrac{x}{2} ight)^2.]

So, let's substitute [MATH: u = \dfrac x 2.] Differentiating, we get [MATH: \dfrac{ extrm{d}u}{ extrm{d}x}= \dfrac{1}{2} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad extrm{d}x =2\, extrm{d}u.]

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and compute it, as follows: [MATH: ∫(1)/(sqrt(4 − x^{2}))dx|= (1)/(4)∫(1)/((x)/(2)sqrt(1 − ((x)/(2))^{2}))dx; = (1)/(4)∫(1)/(usqrt(1 − u^{2})) ⋅ 2du; = (1)/(2)∫(du)/(usqrt(1 − u^{2})); = − (1)/(2)arsech u + C; = − (1)/(2)arsech ((x)/(2)) + C]

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

This integral resembles the basic integral for the inverse hyperbolic cotangent,

[MATH: \int rac{1}{1-u^2}\, extrm{d}u =\arcoth u +C.]

The only difference is that instead of [MATH: u^2] as the variable, we have [MATH: 4x^2 = \left(2x ight)^2.]

So, let's substitute [MATH: u=2x.] Differentiating, we get

[MATH: \dfrac{ extrm{d}u}{ extrm{d}x}=2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac 1 2\, extrm d u = extrm d x.]

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and compute, as follows:

[MATH: ∫(5)/(1 − 4x^{2})dx|= 5∫(1)/(1 − (2x)^{2})dx; = 5∫(1)/(1 − u^{2}) ⋅ (1)/(2)du; = (5)/(2)∫(1)/(1 − u^{2})du; = (5)/(2)arcoth u + C; = (5)/(2)arcoth 2x + C]

Note that this result is subject to the condition [MATH: \left|2x ight| > 1.]

Evaluate the integral [MATH: \displaystyle{\int_{1/9}^{1/6} \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-9x^2}}\, extrm{d}x}.]
EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits}]

Note that we can rewrite this integral as

[MATH: \int_{1/9}^{1/6} \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-9x^2}} \, \textrm{d}x = 3\int_{1/9}^{1/6} \dfrac{1}{3x\sqrt{1-9x^2}}\, \textrm{d}x.]

This integral resembles the basic integral for the inverse hyperbolic secant,

[MATH: \int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-u^2}} \, \textrm{d}u =-\arsech u +C.]

The only difference is that instead of [MATH: u^2] as the variable, we have [MATH: 9x^2 = \left(3x\right)^2.]

So, let's substitute [MATH: u=3x.] Differentiating, we get

[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= 3 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x =\dfrac{1}{3}\,\textrm{d}u.]

Before substituting, we use the table below to change the limits from [MATH: x] to [MATH: u.]

[MATH: x]

[MATH: \dfrac{1}{9}]

[MATH: \dfrac{1}{6}]

[MATH: u]

[MATH: \dfrac{1}{3}]

[MATH: \dfrac{1}{2}]

Using the above, we can now write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and compute it, as follows:

[MATH: \eqalign{ \int_{1/9}^{1/6} \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1 - 9x^2}}\, \textrm{d}x &= 3 \int_{1/9}^{1/6 } \dfrac{1}{3x\sqrt{1 - \left(3x\right)^2}}\, \textrm{d}x \[5pt] &= 3 \int_{1/3}^{1/2} \dfrac{1}{u\sqrt{1 - u^2}}\, \cdot \dfrac{1}{3}\,\textrm{d}u \[5pt] &= \int_{1/3}^{1/2} \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{u \sqrt{1-u^2}} \[5pt] & = - \arsech{u}\Big|_{1/3}^{1/2}\[5pt] &= -\left(\arsech\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - \arsech\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) \right)\[5pt] &= \arsech\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) - \arsech\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) }]

[MATH: \int_{1/9}^{1/6} \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-9x^2}} \, \textrm{d}x = 3\int_{1/9}^{1/6} \dfrac{1}{3x\sqrt{1-9x^2}}\, \textrm{d}x.]

This integral resembles the basic integral for the inverse hyperbolic secant,

[MATH: \int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-u^2}} \, \textrm{d}u =-\arsech u +C.]

The only difference is that instead of [MATH: u^2] as the variable, we have [MATH: 9x^2 = \left(3x\right)^2.]

So, let's substitute [MATH: u=3x.] Differentiating, we get

[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= 3
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\textrm{d}x =\dfrac{1}{3}\,\textrm{d}u.]

Before substituting, we use the table below to change the limits from [MATH: x] to [MATH: u.]

| [MATH: x] | [MATH: \dfrac{1}{9}] | [MATH: \dfrac{1}{6}] |
| [MATH: u] | [MATH: \dfrac{1}{3}] | [MATH: \dfrac{1}{2}] |

Using the above, we can now write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and compute it, as follows:

[MATH: \eqalign{

& = - \arsech{u}\Big|_{1/3}^{1/2}\[5pt]

&= -\left(\arsech\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - \arsech\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) \right)\[5pt]

}]
